title: guard.log times carry their zone, so a machine on another clock reads true
why: Found Nov 1 (local vs cloud audit): shiv's Windows PC runs on Eastern time while the hooks speak Central, and hooks/guard_core.py record() writes datetime.now().isoformat() with no offset, so his guard.log lines read one hour ahead of Central. The batch pace numbers (rule reports-batch-pace-numbers) match guard.log load-brake lines against git times, so on his PC they pick the wrong window.
note: Fix in one home: record() writes the time with its UTC offset (isoformat with tz), and every guard.log reader (lint/guard_log_report.py, the pace read) parses both forms, treating an old line with no offset as zone unknown, never as Central. Red first: a reader test with a +05:00 machine zone. Cloud lane; needs no answer. Done check: a new line carries an offset, and the pace read of an Eastern line lands in the right window. Source: shiv's local audit, bridge session "Claude Code setup audit" (session_013NEJKzvTAwDAZk1K19BoZB, Nov 1 16:40 CST), against this cloud session (triage 5). Placed after ponytail-local-still-on (triage 5).
